NASA SPACE APPS CHALLENGE 2026 · FLAME IN FREEFALL

Smoke or Dust?

The ISS smoke detector misses most Teflon and Kapton smoke. By combining signals the detector already has, our prototype caught 26 of 27 dense smoke tests — versus 19 of 27 for the baseline — with no additional false-alarm tests.

01 / DETECTOR BLIND SPOTS

Where the detector fails

How many dense-smoke tests were caught for each material? The biggest improvements appear for Teflon and Kapton.

Teflon and Kapton produce small smoke particles that can be difficult for light-scattering detectors to detect. Counts reflect the documented five-consecutive-second detection rule.

02 / EXPERIMENT EXPLORER

Explore a real NASA test

Choose any of the 28 tests. The charts show recorded smoke concentration, detector voltage, and out-of-test model predictions from the supplied analysis files.

The ISS 2 V alarm threshold is a planned value documented in NASA's 2005 SAME EIRD, not a verified in-flight setting. STS blank values mean the detector was unavailable, not zero smoke.

03 / OUR MODEL

Four signals. Better coverage.

The prototype combines ISS scattering, ISS beam strength, and two ionization-chamber signals. It was evaluated using leave-one-test-out validation: train on the other 27 tests, then evaluate the held-out test, repeated for all 28.

These bars show the share of dense-smoke seconds detected, not the fraction of whole tests caught. The prototype alarm confidence cutoff is 95%. Reported delay is approximately 4 seconds.

04 / DUST CONTEXT

Smoke versus normal cabin dust

NASA's DAFT experiment provides a cabin dust baseline, while SAME and SAME-R measure smoke. This is a contextual comparison — not a direct dust false-alarm test of our model.

Logarithmic scale; material values are median smoke peaks and DAFT is mean background dust. The 0.3 mg/m³ line is a lunar dust health limit, not a smoke-detector alarm threshold. Different conditions and statistics are shown for context only.

07 / LIMITATIONS

What this prototype does not prove

Only 28 smoke tests were analyzed; 27 reached the defined dense-smoke level (≥2 mg/m³). The ISS 2 V threshold is a planned value from a 2005 document. The 95% model cutoff was selected using these same experiments, so performance on new missions may be lower. There are no paired dust and detector measurements to validate dust rejection. The Kapton 8 false-alarm case may reflect a reference-instrument issue, but this is not confirmed.

Research demonstration only. Not an operational or flight-certified fire safety system.
